1.Nc3 e5 2.Nf3.strategy: Attacks e5 at once and forces Black to defend it. The knight goes to its natural square and White keeps every central set-up open.

1.Nc3 e5 2.d4.strategy: Strikes at e5 straight away and lets Black choose. After the exchange on d4 the queen recaptures and is then hit by a developing move, so White spends a tempo for the open centre, but the extra first move makes up for it.

1.Nc3 e5 2.b3.strategy: Prepares a bishop on the long diagonal, but that diagonal runs through the knight on c3, so the bishop hits nothing until the knight moves. A slow flank move that gives Black time to take the centre.

1.Nc3 e5 2.e3.strategy: A quiet move that opens the king's bishop and prepares a central pawn break, but it makes no claim on the centre at once and lets Black build it freely.

1.Nc3 e5 2.f4.strategy: Offers the f-pawn, but Black takes it and is a clean pawn up. White's only compensation is quick development and a half-open f-file, and with the king's side loosened that is too little.

1.Nc3 e5 2.d4 exd4.strategy: Takes the pawn that attacks e5 and removes White's central pawn. Black accepts open play and lets White's queen come out to recapture.

1.Nc3 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6.strategy: Defends e5 with a developing move and accepts that White chooses the type of game. The centre pawn is held, and Black waits to see whether White strikes at it.

1.Nc3 e5 2.Nf3 Bc5.strategy: Leaves e5 en prise: 3.Nxe5 takes the pawn, and the sacrifice on f2 does not repair it, since after ...Bxf2+ and Kxf2 Black has given a bishop for a pawn. A gambit that gives away a pawn for too little.
1.Nc3 e5 2.Nf3 Bc5.name: Dunst Opening: Billockus-Johansen Gambit
